recipes.name: Mom's Squash Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add squash and onion and cook until tender but still firm, about 15 minutes. Drain and transfer to a 2 quart casserole dish.
In a medium bowl combine soup, cheese and eggs. Mix well and pour into dish with squash.
Bake in preheated oven for 25 minutes. Remove from oven and sprinkle croutons on top. Return to oven and bake for 20 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Mom's Squash Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Yellow squash baked with onion, mushroom soup and Cheddar cheese, with a crouton crust.

review.reviewBody: This was a delicious casserole! I modified it a bit to suit the tastes of my family members. I used a seasoning blend by Pictsweet that has chopped onions, green and red bell peppers, celery, and garlic salt. I sauteed this blend in a little butter while cutting up the squash. I added the squash and water to the sauteed veggies and cooked together for 15 minutes. I substituted cream of celery for the cream of mushroom and added a little cajun seasoning (Tony Chachere's). The casserole came out beautiful and tasted awesome.

I love this recipe! I've had a lot of really beautiful summer squash from my garden this year, and no idea what to do with so much. So I started searching for a recipe that's would utilize a lot at once. And this recipe was perfect for that purpose. Like other reviewers, I did add in my own spices. And instead of boiling, I sautéed the squash and onions in a little bit of extra virgin olive oil, with lots of garlic powder, and some seasoning salt and pepper, until it was tender but still crisp. And after baking it covered for 25 minutes, when I pulled it out to add the breadcrumbs, it seemed a bit dry to me. So I stirred in about 1/4 cup of milk, added a nice layer of Italian bread crumbs to the top, then stuck it back in the oven, uncovered, for an additional 25 mins. It turned out creamy, and delish!! The squash wasn't soggy at all! I'm guessing reviewers that had issues with theyre squash turning out soggy probably over cooked it in the first step. My husband who typically doesn't care for any kind of squash raved about it! Even took some to work in his lunch the day after! My whole family loved it! Thanks for a great recipe! I'll definitely be making it many more times in the future!

I followed this recipe except I sautéed the onions and squash in skillet instead of boiling. Drained. And instead of croutons or bread crumbs on top, I used French Fried Onions (like green bean casserole). It was delicious!!

This was good though had to make changes because of not having mushroom soup on hand. Instead made a white sauce from 2 tbs. butter and 1/4 flour, liquid from small can of mushrooms & and little soy milk until it was the consistancy of canned soup, also added garlic and onion powder. Steamed the squash in the microwave for 5 minutes, twice, draining after each time heated. The squash was still a bit crunchy, and next time will try it for 15 min. in microwave. After putting steamed vegetables in baking dish, spread topping on top. Next time will mix in with the vegetables, as the flavor from sauce and cheese would have been throughout the dish. We did enjoy this and will make it again as posted.

I made this and followed some of the advice of others and sautéed the squash with a tablespoon of butter and the onion and added a clove of garlic instead of boiling. I used butter and garlic croutons to put on top and it was delicious! My husband and I loved it. Followed the rest of the directions.

I just took it out of the oven and my kids flocked to the kitchen. I was short on yellow squash so I added zucchini too. I added some canned potatoes as well. So I can only rate by how I made it. I doubled the recipe. Also, I topped with bread crumbs because my salad eating daughter refused to give up her croutons lol.

A WINNER! I love squash casserole & have been looking for a great recipe for years. It’s hard to find decent recipe without sour cream (as I’m not a big fan). I have tried similar recipes without the egg. THE EGG MAKES THE DIFFERENCE! It adds great texture to the casserole! 
My changes include: adding ½ cup grated carrot for color, stewing the squash, carrots, & onion in butter and chicken broth, adding 3-4 dashes of pepper sauce and garlic powder to the mix for depth of flavor, and using bread crumbs dotted with butter on top instead of croutons. 
SUPER DUPER YUMMY! Try it!

Casserole good as written. However I use chicken stock rather than water & do not add more salt. I reserve the stock after squash & onions have cooked for later use (usually rice!) I change up the topping, sometimes Seasoned Panko Bread Crumbs, crushed Ritz crackers or crushed Pepperidge Farm Herb Seasoned stuffing. But really any topping works. ;-)
I used cream of celery soup and mushrooms, Italian seasoning. I sprinkled a little Romano cheese on the croutons before returning to the oven. We enjoyed it.

This is a good casserole, but it is not as good as the one I lost the recipe for. This recipe is close, but I used ritz crackers instead of croutons as that is what was in my old recipe. I think it would be better if the soup was mixed in with the squash.

This recipe needs a little something extra to give it some zing. I steamed the squash and onion in the microwave in advance so it was very quick to throw this together for a church potluck on Sunday morning. I will definitely make this again, but will likely add minced garlic, salt, pepper, onion powder etc. to add another dimension to the flavor. This recipe will be perfect for a stress free holiday side dish. Thank you!
Really dry. We didn't care for it at all.
We really liked this dish. I did leave out the melted butter on top and substituded it for a can of broccoli cheese soup and then the bread crumbs on top of that.
I tried this recipe and it turned out great. I loved it!
This was a great dish, however I think I will use fried onions next time instead of croutons!
Very easy to put together. A bit too moist at completion but rather tasty. Could use some more herbal additions; will have to experiment with that.
Weird texture, the eggs I think...and not that tasty.
I sauté the onions and steam the squash with some spices rather than boiling them.
So easy and very very good
